reasoning:
Goal: Identify the category and publish date of the bottom (last) post on the homepage. Planned steps and which helpers can help at each step:

1) Enumerate homepage articles in order and obtain the bottom (last) article plus its publish date
- extract_post_summaries: Directly scans '/' main->article nodes and returns per-article dicts including title, date, url and excerpt. It preserves the discovered articles (iteration order matches page order), so selecting the last item yields the bottom post and its publish date. This is the most direct single helper for obtaining the date and permalink.
- compile_recent_posts_digest / export_recent_posts_to_markdown: Also scan the homepage and extract titles/dates into a digest; they can be used to find the bottom post date, but they return Markdown rather than structured rows — still useful but less convenient.
- export_visible_posts_to_csv: Wrapper around extract_post_summaries that ensures reproducible goto and optionally truncates results — useful as a convenience if you prefer the wrapper behavior.

2) Determine the category for that specific bottom post
- search_keyword_group_by_category: Scans the same homepage articles and heuristically finds nearby category anchors (href containing '?cat=' by default) and groups articles by category name. It returns structured mapping category_name -> list of {title,url}. By correlating the bottom post's url (or title) from step 1 with the entries in this grouping, you can determine the bottom post's category. This function implements a heuristic specifically intended for this mapping, so it is the most direct way to discover the visible category for a homepage article.
- export_posts_by_category_date_range: A higher-level helper that calls search_keyword_group_by_category and then fetches posts per-discovered-category (including dates) and writes CSV rows with category,title,date,url. It can therefore produce a direct category->post->date dataset; by searching that output for the bottom post's url/title you can also determine its category and confirm the date. Useful if you want category + date in one pass and CSV output.

3) Fall-back and cross-check
- If extract_post_summaries returns the date but no category, use search_keyword_group_by_category to map the url/title to a category. If the category is not found there, export_posts_by_category_date_range can be tried (it has an 'uncategorized' bucket option) to catch posts missed by the page-nearby-anchor heuristic.

Why other helpers are not selected
- monitor_keyword_and_notify and create_curated_collection_by_search etc. rely on searching or keyword-based filtering and are not aimed at simply mapping the homepage bottom article to its category/date.
- fetch_posts_by_category_and_date_range and export_category_posts_to_csv require you to already know a category name; they are useful downstream (fetch posts once you have a category) but not needed to discover the category of the bottom post.
- duplicate-detection, newsletter wrappers and curated collection wrappers either operate on different goals (duplicates, newsletter composition, search-driven collections) or are convenience wrappers around the selected functions; they are not necessary to accomplish the simple two-field lookup.

Summary of most useful functions to the agent for this task (minimal set):
- extract_post_summaries (primary: get bottom post and its publish date)
- search_keyword_group_by_category (primary: discover category for a given homepage post by URL/title mapping)
- export_posts_by_category_date_range (alternative: single helper that can produce category + date rows for correlation)
- export_visible_posts_to_csv / export_recent_posts_to_markdown / compile_recent_posts_digest (convenience alternatives to obtain dates; less structured than extract_post_summaries but viable)

Recommended workflow (concise):
1. Call extract_post_summaries(page) (or export_visible_posts_to_csv) to get structured list of homepage posts; take the last item -> obtain title, url, date.
2. Call search_keyword_group_by_category(page) and find which category bucket contains the same url/title (or use export_posts_by_category_date_range to get rows containing category,title,date and match by url/title). Return the matched category and the date from step 1.
